ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r4.claim: The form taṣaddā derives from ṣadad, meaning parallel or opposite; its morphological change is regular, and it describes anxiety to convince indifferent people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r4.anchor: it means “parallel” and “opposite.” The change in its morphological form

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p404/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p404/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p404/r1.claim: تصدى means to present oneself toward someone; its root may be صدد, thirst, echo, or opposition.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p404/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p404/r2.speaker: الراعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p404/r2.claim: His verse uses تصدى of turning toward a bright-faced person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p404/r2.anchor: تصدى لوضاح كأن جبينه ... سراج الدجى يجيء إليه الأساور

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.claim: Luxury and self-sufficiency signal rejection and readiness for disbelief and wrongdoing; affliction can purify, humble, and soften hearts, so the more deeply tried are more receptive to fear.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.anchor: الاستغناء والترف أمارة الإعراض وعدم القابلية والتهيؤ للكفر والفجور ، وإلى أن المصائب أمارة للطهارة والإقبال واستكانة القلوب

ELMALILI:80:3-42/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r4.claim: The author reports Bahr's first derivation of tasadda from sadad: the Prophet attends to the man and works for his guidance and reform.

ELMALILI:80:3-42/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r5.claim: Bahr's alternative derives tasadda from sada: the Prophet waits eagerly for the man's response, like expecting an echo from distant mountains.
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r5.anchor: “sen ondan sadâ bekliyor, uzaktan uzağa, dağdan taştan ses in‘ikâsını beklemek gibi

ELMALILI:80:3-42/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r9.claim: Tasadda and talahha are second-person present verbs, shortened from tataṣadda and tatalahha.
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r9.anchor: تَصَدَّىٰ ve تَلَهَّىٰ fiilleri mâzî değil, muzâri‘

RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains taṣaddā as turning toward, approaching, or inclining to someone; its root evokes what stands directly in front of you.
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r1.anchor: أي أنت تقبل عليه وتتعرض له وتميل إليه

RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r2.claim: A reading doubles the ṣād by assimilating the tāʾ into it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r2.anchor: وقرىء : تصدى بالتشديد بإدغام التاء في الصاد

RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r3.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads with ḍamma on the tāʾ: someone draws the Prophet toward addressing the man through his eagerness to secure his Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر : تصدى ، بضم التاء ، أي تعرض

TAB-FULL:v24p107/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p107/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p107/r1.claim: The Prophet attended to the person who considered himself independent through wealth, hoping that he would accept Islam.
TAB-FULL:v24p107/r1.anchor: {أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى} [عبس: 6] قال: نزلت في العباس

TAB-FULL:v24p107/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p107/r2.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v24p107/r2.claim: Sufyan says the passage was revealed concerning al-Abbas.
TAB-FULL:v24p107/r2.anchor: حدثنا ابن حميد، قال: ثنا مهران، عن سفيان، {أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى} [عبس: 6] قال: نزلت في العباس

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.claim: The proposed honorific reading of the switch from third to second person does not fit the direct address that follows, whose rebuke is stronger and has no conciliatory intimacy.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يلائمه الخطاب في قوله بعد { أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى }

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r4.claim: Taṣaddā means turning toward something, engaging with it, and attending to its affairs.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r4.anchor: والتصدي التعرض للشيء بالإقبال عليه والإهتمام بأمره

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.claim: The rebuked pattern is that the Prophet attends to wealthy people who scorn the truth, unconcerned whether they purify themselves, while neglecting the person earnestly seeking purification and fearing God.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.anchor: أنك تعتني وتقبل على من استغنى واستكبر عن اتباع الحق وما عليك أن لا يزكى وتتلهى وتعرض عمن يجتهد في التزكي وهو يخشى

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r12.claim: Fronting anta and the pronouns lahu and ʿanhu emphasizes and fixes the reproach.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r12.anchor: وتقديم ضمير { أنت } في قوله { فأنت له تصدى } وقوله { فأنت عنه تلهى }

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.claim: The verses do not identify the Prophet as the person who frowned; the report leaves its subject unnamed, and the described conduct is incompatible with his character.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.anchor: وليست الآيات ظاهرة الدلالة على أن المراد بها هو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بل خبر محض لم يصرح بالمخبر عنه

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.speaker: المرتضى
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.claim: Al-Murtada is cited for the judgment that attending to the wealthy and neglecting the poor does not resemble the Prophet's noble character.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.anchor: ثم الوصف بأنه يتصدى للأغنياء ويتلهى عن الفقراء لا يشبه أخلاقه الكريمة كما عن المرتضى رحمه الله

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.claim: The Prophet had already been praised for magnificent character in Surat Nun, revealed after the first revelation; this chronology makes a later rebuke for such conduct implausible.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.anchor: وقد عظم الله خلقه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إذ قال

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.claim: Early Meccan commands to warn close kin and lower one's wing to believers further conflict with attributing disdain for the believing poor to the Prophet.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.anchor: فأمره بخفض الجناح للمؤمنين والسورة من السور المكية

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.claim: Early commands forbid longing for worldly goods, require gentleness toward believers, and direct the Prophet to proclaim and turn away from polytheists.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.anchor: وكذا قوله لا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم ولا تحزن عليهم واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.claim: Preferring a rich person's wealth over a poor person's piety by turning away from the poor is rationally ugly and contrary to noble human character, even without an explicit prohibition.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.anchor: قبح عقلي مناف لكريم الخلق الإنساني لا يحتاج في لزوم التجنب عنه إلى نهي لفظي

TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.claim: The claim that the act became sinful only after this moment's prohibition is unsupported; even absent a revealed prohibition, reason judges it ugly and incompatible with the Prophet's praised character.
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن دعوى أنه تعالى لم ينهه إلا في هذا الوقت تحكم ممنوع، ولو سلم فالعقل حاكم

TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.claim: A report from al-Sadiq in al-Majma says the passage concerned an Umayyad man with the Prophet who recoiled, frowned, and turned away when Ibn Umm Maktum arrived; God recounted and condemned it.
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.anchor: أنها نزلت في رجل من بني أمية كان عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فجاء ابن أم مكتوم

TABRISI:80:1-23/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23/r2.speaker: أهل الحجاز
TABRISI:80:1-23/r2.claim: The Hijaz readers geminate the ṣad in تصدى; the others pronounce it lightly.
TABRISI:80:1-23/r2.anchor: وقرأ أهل الحجاز تصدى بالتشديد والباقون تصدى بتخفيف الصاد

TABRISI:80:1-23/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
TABRISI:80:1-23/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir reads تصدى with a prefixed ḍamma and تلهى likewise with a prefixed ḍamma.
TABRISI:80:1-23/r4.anchor: وقراءة أبي جعفر الباقر ع تصدى بضم التاء وفتح الصاد وتلهى بضم التاء أيضا

TABRISI:80:1-23/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23/r8.claim: تصدى means to turn toward or expose oneself to someone; doubling assimilates the deleted initial ta, while the light reading drops one ta from تتصدى.
TABRISI:80:1-23/r8.anchor: أي تعرض فمن قرأ بتشديد الصاد أدغم التاء في الصاد

TABRISI:80:1-23/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23/r12.claim: A reading of تصدى is understood as worldly adornment and tidings drawing one to attend to the wealthy; تلهى correspondingly means turning away from the blind man.
TABRISI:80:1-23/r12.anchor: ومن قرأ تصدى فالمعنى يدعوك داع من زينة الدنيا وبشارتها إلى التصدي له

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r11.claim: تصدى means to approach or attend to the wealthy person.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r11.anchor: أي تتعرض له وتقبل عليه بوجهك

BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r6.claim: Tataṣaddā is shortened by deleting one of its two tāʾs; its full form is tataṣaddā, meaning to turn toward him and devote attention to guiding him.
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r6.anchor: بحذف إحدى التاءين تخفيفا أي تتصدى وتتعرض بالإقبال عليه

BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r7.claim: The Prophet's attentiveness to the self-satisfied man rather than the blind seeker is especially discouraged: a noble person does not eagerly approach someone who turns away.
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r7.anchor: وفيه مزيد تنفير له عليه السلام ، عن مصاحبتهم فإن الإقبال على المدبر

BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r8.claim: Taṣaddī means exposing oneself to something, attending to it, and being preoccupied with it; its opposite is to turn away from it.
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r8.anchor: والتصدي للشيء التعرض والتقيد به والاهتمام بشأنه وضده التشاغل عنه

BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r9.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r9.claim: Al-Mufradāt explains taṣaddī as eager exposure to something, like a thirsty person seeking water.
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r9.anchor: وفي "المفردات" التصدي التعرض للشيء على حرص كتعرض الصديان

BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r10.claim: Some derive taṣaddī from ṣadad, what faces or confronts one, with one of the doubled letters replaced by a weak letter.
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r10.anchor: وعن بعضهم أصل تصدي تصدد من الصدد وهو ما استقبلك وجاء قبالتك

THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked for instruction while the Prophet addressed Quraysh leaders; the Prophet turned from him, thinking the elite might reject a following of blind, poor, and enslaved people.
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.anchor: أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r1.claim: The Prophet turns toward and attends to the wealthy man.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r1.anchor: { فأنت له تصدى } تقبل عليه وتتعرض له.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r10.claim: The context identifies the person to whom the Prophet was turning his attention as one of the wealthy pagan leaders being courted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r10.anchor: Hz. Peygamber putperest önderlerin ikna edilmesi halinde onları izleyen halkın İslâm’ı daha kolay benimseyecekleri düşüncesiyle onlarla da meşgul oluyordu

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r12.claim: To attend to him means to turn one's face toward him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r12.anchor: فأنت له تصدى ، أي تقبل عليه بوجهك

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.claim: The whole passage is a reproach directed to the Prophet on behalf of the poor.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.anchor: وهذا كله من قبيل العتاب معه لأجل الفقراء

SULAMI:v2p373#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r1.claim: Abū ʿUthmān says God commanded the Prophet to keep company with the poor.
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : أمر الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بمجالسة الفقراء

SULAMI:v2p373#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r2.claim: Abū ʿUthmān says God urged the Prophet to honor the poor.
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : أمر الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بمجالسة الفقراء وحثه على تعظيمهم

SULAMI:v2p373#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r3.claim: Abū ʿUthmān says God forbade the Prophet from loving the wealthy.
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r3.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : أمر الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بمجالسة الفقراء وحثه على تعظيمهم ونهاه عن محبة الأغنياء

DAMGHANI:v1p274/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r11.claim: Taṣaddā means turning one's face toward someone.
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r11.anchor: فأنت له تصدى تقبل بوجهك عليه

FARRA:v3p235/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p235/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p235/r8.claim: A reader's recitation تصدى is also correct.

NAHHAS:v5p149/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p149/r12.speaker: المدنيون
NAHHAS:v5p149/r12.claim: The Medinan reading reflects the original تتصدى with the two tāʾs assimilated.
NAHHAS:v5p149/r12.anchor: قراءة المدنيين والأصل تتصدى ثم أدغم

NAHHAS:v5p149/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p149/r13.speaker: الكوفيون وأبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v5p149/r13.claim: The Kufans and Abu Amr read تصدى, deleting a tāʾ to avoid two consecutive tāʾs.
NAHHAS:v5p149/r13.anchor: وقراءة الكوفيين وأبي عمرو ( تصدى ) بحذف التاء لئلا يجمع بين تاءين

SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r1.claim: The word has previously discussed heavy and light readings; both carry the sense of exposing oneself or attending to someone.
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r1.anchor: فيه قراءتا التثقيل والتخفيف، ومعناه تتعرض

SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r2.claim: The usual derivation is from الصدد, what faces you; the original تصدد lost one identical consonant as a weak letter to avoid gemination, as in تظنيت, قصيت أظفاري and the poetic تقضي.
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r2.anchor: وأصله تصدد من الصدد، وهو ما استقبلك وصار قبالتك، فأبدل أحد الأمثال حرف علة نحو: تظنيت وقصيت أظفاري و: 4498 تقضي البازي

SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r3.claim: Another derivation is from الصدى, an echo or sound heard in empty places and hard objects; deriving the sense of exposure from it is strained.
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو من الصدى، وهو الصوت المسموع في الأماكن الخالية والأجرام الصلبة

SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r4.claim: A further derivation is from الصدى meaning thirst; the author says the exposure sense must be forced if this is the root.
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r4.anchor: وقيل: من الصدى وهو العطش، والمعنى على التعرض، ويتمحل لذلك إذا قلنا: أصله من الصوت أو العطش

SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r5.claim: The cited anonymous poem uses تصدى in the sense of presenting oneself or attending to someone, describing a radiant-faced person approached by ornaments.
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر: 4499 تصدى لوضاح كأن جبينه سراج الدجى تجبى إليه الأساور

SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r6.claim: Abu Jafar reads تصدى with a damma on ت and a light ص; the author explains it as your being prompted toward him, with the verb used both intransitively and transitively.
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر " تصدى " بضم التاء وتخفيف الصاد، أي: تصديك يحرضك على إسلامه. يقال: تصدى الرجل وتصديته

SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the damma reading as exposure to him: a caller's zeal and intense eagerness for his conversion impels you to attend to him.
SAMIN-DURR:80:6/r7.anchor: وقرىء " تصدى " بضم التاء، أي: تعرض، ومعناه: يدعوك داع إلى التصدي له من الحرص والتهالك على إسلامه

ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r1.claim: The addressee attends to the person who considers himself self-sufficient.

ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r2.claim: With light ṣād, taṣaddā derives from tataṣaddā, with the second tāʾ deleted where two tāʾs meet.
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r2.anchor: فمن قرأ (تصدى) - بتخفيف الصاد - فالأصل تتصدى

ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r3.claim: Another reading assimilates the tāʾ into ṣād; its underlying form and meaning are also tataṣaddā.
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r3.anchor: ومن قرأ (تصدى) بإدغام التاء، فالمعنى أيضا تتصدى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.claim: ʿAbasa pairs with al-Nāziʿāt and shares its central theme, discourse style, and reasoning; the changed sequence of topics gives this sūrah its distinct majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.anchor: There is no basic difference between the central theme of both sūrahs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.claim: Though the Prophet is addressed in the rebuke, its intended target is the haughty leaders who ignore his message and want poor companions excluded to secure their own attendance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.anchor: Although the Prophet (sws) is addressed, yet the direction of this stern address is towards these supercilious people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.claim: The Prophet's responsibility is to teach those who come eagerly, including devoted companions, rather than pamper absent leaders; he is not accountable for those who refuse to come.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.anchor: His real responsibility is to educate and instruct only those who come to him enthusiastically.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Nāfiʿ read تصدى with a doubled ṣād.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع: تصدى [عبس/ 6] مشددة الصاد

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r2.claim: The remaining readers use a light ṣād in تصدى.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses تصدي as تعرض, meaning to turn or present oneself toward someone.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r4.speaker: ذو الرمة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r4.claim: Dhū al-Rumma’s line is cited for تصدى as turning toward; al-Fārisī quotes it as poetic evidence for the gloss تعرض.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r4.anchor: قال ذو الرمة : ترى القلوة القوداء فيها كفارك تصدى لعينيها فصدت حليلها

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says القلوة is the mare that follows the colt, and explains that she turns toward her mate, who turns away.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r5.anchor: يعني بالقلوة التي تتبع القلو. قال: يريد تصدى حليلها فصدت

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r6.claim: The doubled ṣād comes from assimilating the tāʾ of تتصدى into ṣād.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r6.anchor: من قال: تصدى أدغم التاء في الصاد

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r7.claim: The light ṣād is analyzed as تتصدى with its extra tāʾ deleted rather than assimilated.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p376#2/r7.anchor: ومن قال: تصدى أراد تتصدى فحذف التاء ولم يدغمها

QIRAAT-ER:80:6:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:80:6:4#1/r1.speaker: Assim
QIRAAT-ER:80:6:4#1/r1.claim: Assimilation intensifies the onset and compresses the underlying taṣaddā sequence in recitation.
QIRAAT-ER:80:6:4#1/r1.anchor: Assim, mutawatir: Canonical assimilation intensifies the consonantal onset, making the underlying taṣaddā sequence more compressed in recitation

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r2.speaker: الحرميان وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r2.claim: The two Medinan readers and Abū ʿAmr, with the stated qualification, double the zāy and ṣād; the rest of the Seven lighten them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r2.anchor:
وقرأ الحرميان وأبو عمرو: بخلاف تزكى وتصدى، بشد الزاي والصاد وباقي السبعة:
بخفها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r1.claim: The Prophet attends to and approaches the self-satisfied man, eager to guide and reform him; pursuing someone who turns away is unbecoming, as the cited verse says.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r1.anchor: أي تتصدى وتتعرض بالإقبال عليه والأهتمام بإرشاده واستصلاحه وفيه مزيد تنفير له صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن مصاحبتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r2.claim: The accompanying verse says it is improper to seek the company of someone who rejects yours.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r2.anchor: ومن هنا قيل لا أبتغي وصل من لا يبتغي صلتي ولا ألين لمن لا يبتغي ليني

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r3.speaker: الحرميان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r3.claim: The two Meccan readers double ṣād, from tataṣaddā with the tāʾ changed to ṣād and assimilated.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان تصدى بتشديد الصاد على أن الأصل تتصدى فقلبت التاء صادا وأدغمت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the verb passive with a ḍamma and light ṣād: ‘you are directed to attend to him,’ by an inner agent of eagerness for his conversion.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر تصدى بضم التاء وتخفيف الصاد مبنيا للمفعول أي تعرض ومعناه يدعوك إلى التصدي والتعرض له داع من الحرص

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r5.claim: The root may be ṣadad, something facing you, as in one house facing another; alternatives derive it from thirst or from the familiar word for echo.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#3/r5.anchor: وأصل تصدى على ما في البحر تصدد من الصدد وهو ما استقبلك وصار قبالتك يقال داري صدد داره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r6.claim: The Prophet turns toward this person, attends to him, and listens to what he says.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r6.anchor: تتعرض له وتقبل عليه وتصغي إلى كلامه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r7.speaker: أهل الحجاز، والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r7.claim: The Hijaz readers double the ṣād by assimilation, meaning تتصدى; the others lighten it through deletion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r7.anchor: وقرأ أهل الحجاز: "تصدى" بتشديد الصاد على الإدغام، أي: تتصدى، وقرأ الآخرون

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r6.claim: The verb means you attend to him; its underlying form is tataṣaddā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r6.anchor: تتعرض له بالإقبال عليه وأصله تتصدى

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r7.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir and Nafi read the form with assimilation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r8.claim: A further reading can mean either that you turn toward him or that you are summoned to attend to him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r8.anchor: وقرىء. «تصدى» أي تعرض وتدعى إلى التصدي.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r15.claim: The Prophet devoted himself to exhorting the wealthy man rather than the blind visitor, hoping he and his followers would convert; the chiefs included ʿUtba, Abū Jahl, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r15.anchor: وهم عتبة بن ربيعة وأبو جهل وأبي وأمية ابنا خلق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r16.claim: The majority omit the tāʾ of the form, while Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr assimilate it; the light form signals that the action was slight.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r16.anchor: وأشار حذف تاء التفعل في قراءة الجماعة وإدغامها في قراءة نافع وابن كثير إلى أن ذلك كان على وجه خفيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r10.claim: Ammā means ‘whatever may occur’; whenever a self-sufficient person exists, the Prophet turns to him, with the conditional attachment exaggerating his persistent attention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r10.anchor: تقدم الكلام على { أما } في سورة النازعات أنها بمعنى : مهما يكن شيء ، فقوله : { أما من استغنى } تفسيره مهما يكن الذي استغنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r2.claim: The explicit subject pronoun before the verb may strengthen the rebuke: ‘you’ attend to him with particular intensity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r2.anchor: والإتيان بضمير المخاطب مظهرا قبل المسند الفعلي دون استتاره في الفعل يجوز أن يكون للتقوي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r3.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun may restrict the action to the Prophet: this attention was unbecoming to his high rank, though less blameworthy from another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفيدا للاختصاص ، أي فأنت لا غيرك تتصدى له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r4.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū Jaʿfar read with a doubled ṣād, assimilating one tāʾ into it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو جعفر بفتح التاء وتشديد الصاد على إدغام إحدى التاءين في الصاد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r5.speaker: الباقون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r5.claim: The other readers use a light ṣād, deleting one of the two tāʾs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r5.anchor: والباقون بالفتح وتخفيف الصاد على حذف إحدى التاءين .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r6.claim: Taṣaddī means turning toward or exposing oneself; here it is a metaphor for strong attention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r6.anchor: والتصدي : التعرض ، أطلق هنا على الإقبال الشديد مجازا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r7.claim: The sentence is parenthetical between the two ‘as for’ clauses, and its wāw is parenthetical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r7.anchor: جملة معترضة بين جملة { أما من استغنى } ( عبس : 5 ) وجملة : { وأما من جاءك يسعى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r10.claim: Ammā means ‘whatever may occur’; whenever a self-sufficient person exists, the Prophet turns to him, with the conditional attachment exaggerating his persistent attention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r10.anchor: تقدم الكلام على { أما } في سورة النازعات أنها بمعنى : مهما يكن شيء ، فقوله : { أما من استغنى } تفسيره مهما يكن الذي استغنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r2.claim: The explicit subject pronoun before the verb may intensify the action: the reproach targets the Prophet’s forceful attention to the affluent man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r2.anchor: الإتيان بضمير المخاطب مظهرا قبل المسند الفعلي دون استتاره في الفعل يجوز أن يكون للتقوي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r3.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun restricts the action to the Prophet: such attention is inappropriate to his high station, though it would be minor from someone else.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفيدا للاختصاص ، أي فأنت لا غيرك تتصدى له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r4.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū Jaʿfar read with a doubled ṣād, assimilating one of the two tāʾs into it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو جعفر بفتح التاء وتشديد الصاد على إدغام إحدى التاءين في الصاد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r5.speaker: الباقون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r5.claim: The remaining readers use a light ṣād, deleting one of the two tāʾs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r5.anchor: والباقون بالفتح وتخفيف الصاد على حذف إحدى التاءين .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r6.claim: Taṣaddī means turning toward or exposing oneself; here it metaphorically denotes giving someone intense attention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r6.anchor: والتصدي : التعرض ، أطلق هنا على الإقبال الشديد مجازا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r7.claim: This clause is parenthetical between the contrast about the self-sufficient person and the clause about the eager visitor; the wāw is parenthetical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r7.anchor: جملة معترضة بين جملة { أما من استغنى } ( عبس : 5 ) وجملة : { وأما من جاءك يسعى } ( عبس : 8 ) ، والواو اعتراضية .

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Nāfiʿ read taṣaddā with a doubled ṣād.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع تصدى بتشديد الصاد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r2.speaker: عاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read it with an open tāʾ and ṣād and a light ṣād.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي تصدى بفتح التاء والصاد وتخفيفها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب وأبو الجوزاء وعمرو بن دينار
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Abū al-Jawzāʾ, and ʿAmr ibn Dīnār read tataṣaddā with two tāʾs and a light ṣād.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب وأبو الجوزاء وعمرو بن دينار تتصدى بتاءين مع تخفيف الصاد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the underlying form is tataṣaddā, with the second tāʾ dropped because two tāʾs meet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج الأصل تتصدى ولكن حذفت التاء الثانية لاجتماع تاءين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r5.claim: The assimilated reading still means tataṣaddā, with tāʾ assimilated into ṣād because their articulation points are close.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r5.anchor: ومن قرأ تصدى بإدغام التاء فالمعنى أيضا تتصدى إلا أن التاء أدغمت في الصاد لقرب مخرج التاء من الصاد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as turning toward someone with one's face.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس تصدى تقبل عليه بوجهك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the verb as making oneself available or approaching.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن السميفع والجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ, and al-Jaḥdarī read it with one damma-marked tāʾ and a light ṣād.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#5/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابن السميفع والجحدري تصدى بتاء واحدة مضمومة وتخفيف الصاد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.claim: The self-sufficient person is the rich man whom the Prophet approached in hope of guidance, though he was not accountable if the man failed to purify himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.anchor: أي: أما الغني فأنت تتعرض له لعله يهتدي،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.claim: God directs the Prophet to warn everyone equally, without favoring the eminent over the weak, rich over poor, masters over slaves, men over women, or adults over children; God guides whom He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.anchor: ومن هاهنا أمر الله عز وجل رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا يخص بالإنذار أحدا، بل يساوي فيه بين الشريف والضعيف، والفقير والغني، والسادة والعبيد،

JISHUMI:v10p7279/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, and Ibn Kathīr read taṣaddā with a doubled ṣād through assimilation from tataṣaddā; the other readers have a light ṣād after dropping the second tāʾ.
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير: تصدى بتشديد الصاد على الإدغام، وأصله تتصدى

JISHUMI:v10p7279/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r10.claim: Taṣaddī means exposing oneself to something as a thirsty person approaches water; ṣadā is thirst, and the word also means to look expectantly toward something.
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r10.anchor: والتصدي: التعرض للشيء كتعرض العطشان للماء، وأصل الصدى العطش

JISHUMI:v10p7279/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r11.claim: The word ṣadā, echo, is explained either by dryness like a thirsty throat or by the echo's seeming to present speech by returning something like it.
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r11.anchor: وسمي الصدى؛ لأنه بالجفاف صار كجفاف حلق العطشان

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r11.claim: Taṣaddā means approaching the wealthy person, listening to him, and turning toward him while turning away from the poor.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r11.anchor: قيل: تتعرض له، وتصغي إلى كلامه، وتقبل عليه بوجهك، وتعرض عن الفقير،

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r12.claim: Alternatively, taṣaddā derives from ṣadā, ‘echo,’ and means that you address him.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r12.anchor: وقيل: تصدى من الصدى، وهو الصوت؛ أي: تخاطبه.

MUQATIL:80:1-7/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r7.claim: The Prophet turns toward the self-sufficient man and invites him.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#4/r1.claim: You turn your attention toward him, eager for him to believe.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#4/r1.anchor: تتعرض بالاقبال عليه حرصا على إيمانه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#4/r2.speaker: حجازى
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#4/r2.claim: A Hijazi reading assimilates the tāʾ into the ṣād in تصدى.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#4/r2.anchor: بالاقبال عليه حرصا على إيمانه تصدى بادغام التاء فى الصاد حجازى

QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r2.claim: Taṣaddā means to turn toward someone and listen attentively to what he says.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r2.anchor: { فأنت له تصدى } أي تعرض له، وتصغي لكلامه. والتصدي: الإصغاء قال الراعي

QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r3.speaker: الراعي
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r3.claim: Al-Ra'i's verse illustrates taṣaddā as leaning or attending toward a person.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r3.anchor: قال الراعي: تصدى لوضاح كأن جبينه سراج الدجى يحني إليه الأساور

QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r4.claim: One etymology derives taṣaddā from ṣadd, what faces or stands opposite; “my house is ṣadad his house” means directly opposite it.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r4.anchor: وأصله تتصدد من الصد، وهو ما استقبلك، وصار قبالتك يقال: داري صدد داره

QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r5.claim: Another derivation relates it to ṣadā, thirst: the Prophet approaches the man as a thirsty person approaches water; muṣādāh can also mean opposition.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r5.anchor: وقيل: من الصدى وهو العطش. أي تتعرض له كما يتعرض العطشان للماء، والمصاداة: المعارضة

QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r6.claim: The common reading has the light form, dropping the second tā for ease of pronunciation.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r6.anchor: وقراءة العامة «تصدى» بالتخفيف، على طرح التاء الثانية تخفيفا

QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r7.speaker: نافع وابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r7.claim: Nafi and Ibn Muhaysin read the form with gemination through assimilation.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن محيض بالتشديد على الإدغام

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads تصدى with ḍamma on tāʾ and a light ṣād; Ibn Jinnī explains that worldly adornment draws the Prophet to turn toward and attend to the wealthy man.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p352/r4.anchor: معنى "تصدى"، أي: يدعوك داع من زينة الدنيا وشارتها

NASHR:v2p397#2/r19.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p397#2/r19.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير
NASHR:v2p397#2/r19.claim: The two Medinan readers and Ibn Kathīr geminate the ṣād in تصدى.
NASHR:v2p397#2/r19.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان، وابن كثير بتشديد الصاد، وقرأ الباقون بتخفيفها،

NASHR:v2p397#2/r20.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p397#2/r20.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p397#2/r20.claim: The remaining readers pronounce the ṣād in تصدى without gemination.
NASHR:v2p397#2/r20.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان، وابن كثير بتشديد الصاد، وقرأ الباقون بتخفيفها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r3.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة والأعرج وعيسى والأعمش وجمهور السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r3.claim: These readers use a light ṣād in taṣaddā, derived from yataṣaddā with deletion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة والأعرج وعيسى والأعمش وجمهور السبعة: تصدى بخف الصاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r4.speaker: الحرميان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r4.claim: The two readers of the Haramain geminate the ṣād by assimilating the tāʾ into it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r4.anchor: والحرميان: بشدها، أدغم التاء في الصاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r5.claim: Abu Ja'far reads with a damma on the tāʾ and light ṣād, interpreted as the Prophet being diverted by eagerness for the man's conversion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r5.anchor: وأبو جعفر: تصدى، بضم التاء وتخفيف الصاد، أي يصدك حرصك على إسلامه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r6.claim: The self-sufficient man is variously identified as al-Walid, Umayya, Utba and Shayba, or Umayya together with those named in the occasion report.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r6.anchor: وهذا المستغني هو الوليد، أو أمية، أو عتبة وشيبة، أو أمية وجميع المذكورين في سبب النزول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r7.speaker: القرطبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the interpreters are mistaken because Umayya and al-Walid were in Mecca while Ibn Umm Maktum was in Medina; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because the sura is Meccan and all were in Mecca at revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r7.anchor: قال القرطبي: وهذا كله غلط من المفسرين، لأنه أمية والوليد كانا بمكة، وابن أم مكتوم كان بالمدينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Ibn Umm Maktum was first in Mecca before emigrating, and identifies him as Abdullah ibn Sarh ibn Malik ibn Rabi'a al-Fihri, of Banu Amir ibn Lu'ayy, cousin of Khadija; Umm Maktum was his paternal grandmother Atika.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r8.anchor: وكانوا جميعهم بمكة حين نزول هذه الآية. وابن أم مكتوم هو عبد الله بن سرح بن مالك بن ربيعة الفهري

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.claim: In another account, ʿAʾisha says the Prophet was addressing Quraysh leaders including Abu Jahl and ʿUtba when Ibn Umm Maktum came; the Prophet turned away, and the quoted passage was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مجلس من ناس من وجوه قريش منهم أبو جهل بن هشام وعتبة بن ربيعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r8.claim: تصدى means that the Prophet turns or exposes himself toward the person.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r9.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir and Nafi read the form with a doubled ṣād, assimilating the tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع: «تصدى» بشد الصاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r10.speaker: الباقون والأعرج والحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة وعيسى والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r10.claim: The remaining readers and the listed authorities read it with a light ṣād after dropping the tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r10.anchor: وقرأ الباقون والأعرج والحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة وعيسى والأعمش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر بن القعقاع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r11.claim: Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa reads it with a damma on tāʾ and a light ṣād as a passive form, meaning the Prophet's concern for disbelievers causes him to turn toward them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بن القعقاع: «تصدى» ، بضم التاء وتخفيف الصاد
